pue.boundary: Supplier silicon, networking and rack content; Broadcom does not operate the matched customer compute-energy perimeter
pue.basis: PUE is matched facility energy divided by IT-equipment energy. It is not a supplier attribute. Customer-site operational PUE for the revenue cohort is not disclosed, so no low/base/high deployment range is invented.

model.revenue_scope: Reported $16.7B recognized AI semiconductor revenue combines custom accelerators and AI networking. It excludes infrastructure software but does not separately disclose custom accelerator, networking or full-rack pass-through content.
model.capacity_time_basis: No period-average active IT-load denominator is reconstructed. The more-than-1GW XPV tranche, more-than-1GW Meta commitment and 10GW OpenAI collaboration are future announced capacity, not the Q3 delivered revenue cohort.

formulas.XPV_max_backstop_density_upper_bound: 29B / more_than_1_stated_compute_GW; therefore less than 29B per stated compute GW
formulas.operator_revenue_per_effective_utilized_: not_applicable to supplier revenue; an operator model would require annualized attributable recognized compute revenue / time-weighted active IT MW / physical utilization / 1e6
formulas.deployment_PUE: sum(matched_facility_energy) / sum(matched_IT_equipment_energy); IT-energy weighted across sites and periods
formulas.conditional_utilization_sensitivity: If a future operator numerator and verified active IT MW are disclosed, rate = annualized_attributable_revenue / (active_IT_MW * physical_utilization) / 1e6. PUE applies only when converting matching facility power/energy to IT load/energy.

structured_deals.economic_effect: $126.821B, primarily inventory, versus $0.132B at FY2025 year-end. $52.674B falls in FY2027 and $72.952B in FY2028. The filing excludes cancelable agreements and unconditional obligations with one year or less remaining. This is a purchase-commitment stock, not capex paid or recognized revenue.

structured_deals.status: Initial $35B transaction announced 2026-06-09; deployment expected from mid-2026
structured_deals.economic_effect: Private capital funds AI racks and leases compute to the customer. Broadcom gives a five-year lease backstop that ramps with delivery and falls with customer payments; full-deployment maximum is about $29B undiscounted. Default exposure is 85% of outstanding backstopped lease amounts less rack resale value, with lease-assumption and sale remedies. Transaction value and stated GW are not Broadcom revenue or active Q3 IT load.

findings: Broadcom reported $16.7B of Q3 AI semiconductor revenue, up 221% year over year and 54% sequentially. It equals 56.4% of consolidated revenue and roughly 80.1% of semiconductor-segment revenue, but the public release combines custom accelerators and networking.

Legally binding purchase commitments rose from $0.132B at FY2025 year-end to $126.821B at 2026-08-02, a 960.8x stock-date increase. The vast majority falls in FY2027-FY2028 and is primarily inventory.

The XPV platform moves rack funding to Apollo, Blackstone and banks but leaves Broadcom with an approximately $29B undiscounted maximum lease backstop after full deployment. That cap is about 1.21x Broadcom's $23.975B quarter-end cash; it is not an expected loss and benefits from rack collateral and contractual remedies.

RPO reached $179.2B and includes a long-term custom accelerator contract; approximately 25% is expected in the next 12 months. RPO, the $35B XPV tranche and the potential $42B customer notes remain distinct from recognized revenue.

Supplier PUE is not applicable. Customer-site PUE, physical utilization and the Q3 matched deployed IT-load denominator are not disclosed, so the prior compiled anchor is superseded and no revenue-per-effective-MW range is published.

Top-five end-customer concentration rose to approximately 55% of Q3 revenue from approximately 40% a year earlier. Broadcom also warns that custom inventory may not be resellable and that customer power, water and financing constraints can delay deployments.
gaps: Exact Q3 accelerator-versus-networking revenue split, full-rack pass-through content and customer identities by recognized-revenue cohort.
Opening, activation-dated and period-average deployed IT-load GW corresponding to Q3 recognized AI semiconductor revenue; announced future GW cannot substitute.
Customer-site matched facility energy, IT-equipment energy, IT-energy weights and physical utilization; no defensible operational PUE or effective-utilized denominator.
Supplier/counterparty allocation of the $126.821B purchase commitments, cancellation/rescheduling economics, prepayments, wafer/packaging terms and inventory obsolescence protection.

XPV executed purchase, lease and credit agreements; exact customer; draw schedule; interest/lease rates; collateral ownership; rack resale assumptions; default triggers; recovery waterfall and replacement schedule.
Recognized revenue and gross-margin accounting for Broadcom silicon, networking and possible full-rack sales under XPV; risk-factor language says full racks may lower gross margin and cash flow.
No matched realized token price, task volume, energy per task or workload mix supports an exact Jevons break-even or open-versus-proprietary model comparison.
